question.text: Syndicate ABC LLP committed INR 25 crore (lead Mr. A: INR 5 cr; other accredited LPs: INR 20 cr) with 15% carry to the lead. Exit is INR 75 crore after 3 years. After computing the lead's carry (INR 7.50 crore on INR 50 crore profit), the REMAINING distribution of INR 67.50 crore is split pro-rata based on committed capital. How much does Mr. A receive in TOTAL (his carry + his pro-rata share as an LP)?

answer.text: INR 21.00 crore (carry INR 7.50 cr + pro-rata INR 13.50 cr)
INR 13.50 crore (pro-rata only, ignoring the lead's carry)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the AIF Managers workbook syndicate example (p. 258), the calculation proceeds in three steps. Step 1: Exit proceeds equal INR 75 crore on committed capital of INR 25 crore, so profit equals INR 50 crore. Carry to the lead equals 15 percent of INR 50 crore, that is INR 7.50 crore. Step 2: The remaining INR 75 crore minus INR 7.50 crore, that is INR 67.50 crore, is distributed pro-rata by committed capital. Mr. A's pro-rata share equals (5 / 25) times INR 67.50 crore, that is INR 13.50 crore. Step 3: Mr. A's total equals INR 7.50 crore in carry plus INR 13.50 crore in pro-rata, that is INR 21.00 crore. The Trap: INR 7.50 crore captures only the lead's carry and ignores Mr. A's pro-rata participation as an LP. INR 13.50 crore captures only the pro-rata share and ignores the carry. INR 25.00 crore is the entire post-carry pool and overstates Mr. A's entitlement by treating him as the sole pro-rata recipient. Note: The 15 percent carry on INR 50 crore profit gives INR 7.50 crore, and (5 / 25) times INR 67.50 crore gives INR 13.50 crore; the sum is INR 21.00 crore.
